correctness.rationale: For any adaptive strategy, each unvisited count changes by at most one per scheduled visit, and its success threshold is bounded above by eps+(1-eps)k/m. A shared-uniform coupling prevents the greedy count exceeding a competitor count, coordinatewise; this proves stochastic, not merely expectation, dominance. Greedy alternates independent side-specific coupon chains, initial missing counts m and m-1, with p_m=1, hence tau=max(2S_B-1,2(S_A-1)) and the exact odd/even CDF. The geometric Laplace product is a gamma quotient with a=m eps/(1-eps), delta=m(expm1(s/m))/(1-eps). In the critical window a->c, delta->s, (delta-s)log m->0; mgfs around zero give -log Gamma(c+1,1). In the diffuse window integral sums yield variance asymptotic m/eps and Lyapunov ratio O((m eps)^(-1/2)+(m eps)^(-3/2)); independent two-clock maxima give Phi^2. Replay of the standalone checker gave 906 passed finite and transform assertions. Residual risk: mathematical indexing mistakes outside tested cases; no finite-only inference.

value.rationale: A complete stochastically optimal law for all sizes and steering rates is a natural sharp benchmark for general adaptive graph-coverage questions. The epsilon~1/m window yields continuously indexed negative-log-gamma fluctuations with explicit two-side maximum; in the larger vanishing-epsilon window the one-side clocks become asymptotically normal but their maximum remains nonnormal. This is not a renamed expected-time inequality or a known tabular recomputation; neither law nor its structural two-phase distinction follows from the general cover-time bounds. The narrow family is mathematically canonical (degree-m balanced complete bipartite graphs), and its full exact optimality is an object-level motivation.
